nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Asks for the AI provider and model and the browser and device, because the app runs almost entirely client-side against a user-chosen provider, so those two facts determine reproducibility more than any server state.

nodes.label: Feature Request Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Asks who the feature helps, with final-year students applying for placements given as the example, keeping proposals anchored to the target user rather than to generic product value.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checklist Template
nodes.rationale: Six boxes condensing the CLAUDE.md checklist: checks pass, no student data or keys reach the server (invariants 1-2), no paid service or always-on server, no secrets in the diff, opened it in a browser and used the thing changed, and docs updated.

nodes.label: CI check Job
nodes.rationale: Runs on push to main and every pull request: checkout, setup-node pinned from .nvmrc with npm cache, npm ci, tsc --noEmit, lint, build. Deliberately limited to types, lint and build, which is why the docs insist green CI is not evidence a change works.

nodes.label: Claude review Job
nodes.rationale: Runs anthropics/claude-code-action on PR opened and synchronize with a prompt that walks the CLAUDE.md pre-merge checklist and review priority order, flags broken invariants by number, and is instructed not to approve or merge and to say plainly what it could not verify.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Gate Step
nodes.rationale: A shell step writes enabled=true/false to GITHUB_OUTPUT depending on whether the secret exists, and every later step is conditioned on it, so the job skips cleanly on forks instead of failing and never spends credit that was not opted into.

nodes.label: What the Server Sees
nodes.rationale: With a student's own key the server sees nothing beyond static files and the trending feed. Written as what a host can truthfully tell students, so the claim is bounded by what the architecture actually guarantees.

nodes.label: Shared-Key Data Handling Disclosure
nodes.rationale: The prompt passes through /api/generate once, is forwarded to Google Gemini, and is streamed back with Cache-Control: no-store, never written to logs and never stored. Vercel's own request logs hold URL, status and timing but not request bodies, and that distinction is stated rather than glossed.

nodes.label: Anonymous Device Id and IP Counting
nodes.rationale: A random per-browser UUID plus the requester IP are used solely to count requests against the shared key's daily limits; with Upstash the counters live in Redis and expire after about 26 hours. The id is anonymous and header-only so fair rate limiting does not require identifying the student.
nodes.norm_label: anonymous device id and ip counting

nodes.label: What the Browser Stores
nodes.rationale: Defers to the README privacy table rather than duplicating it, noting the 48-hour TTL enforced on app load and the Clear all my data button.

nodes.label: Host Prohibitions
nodes.rationale: Three things a host must not do: add analytics that capture page content or inputs, log request bodies in /api/generate, or move keys and drafts to a server without adding real authentication first. Each maps to a specific invariant that would otherwise be broken silently by a well-meaning operational change.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — repo instructions for AI and human contributors
nodes.rationale: Written as the short version of how the project stays free, private and easy to fork; humans are told to read it too, not only Claude Code.
nodes.norm_label: claude.md — repo instructions for ai and human contributors

nodes.label: The three founding constraints
nodes.rationale: The whole design follows from three constraints; a change that breaks one is the wrong change however good the feature is.

nodes.label: Constraint 1: it must cost the host zero rupees
nodes.rationale: Vercel Hobby, free-tier AI keys, no database, no paid add-ons — so anyone can fork and host it for a college without a card.
nodes.norm_label: constraint 1: it must cost the host zero rupees

nodes.label: Constraint 2: student data must never reach the server
nodes.rationale: Profiles, resumes, drafts and API keys live in the browser, so there is nothing server-side that can leak.
nodes.norm_label: constraint 2: student data must never reach the server

nodes.label: Constraint 3: usable in under two minutes with no account
nodes.rationale: Target user is a student on a shared lab computer; any account gate or setup ceremony defeats the product.
nodes.norm_label: constraint 3: usable in under two minutes with no account

nodes.label: Hard invariants (twelve, never break these)
nodes.rationale: Twelve numbered rows, each with its own stated Why, form the merge gate the pre-merge checklist and PR review both check against.

nodes.label: Invariant 1: BYOK calls go browser to provider directly
nodes.rationale: A student's API key must never be sent to our server, logged, or put in a URL: if the server never holds it, it cannot leak it.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 1: byok calls go browser to provider directly

nodes.label: Invariant 2: student content stays client-side
nodes.rationale: Profile text, resume text and drafts live in IndexedDB or component state; the single exception is the shared-key proxy, which forwards one prompt to Gemini and stores nothing. This is the product's promise, stated in the README and in-app.

nodes.label: Invariant 3: no server-side database, no accounts, no auth
nodes.rationale: Holding resumes and keys server-side without real auth is a liability, and an account gate breaks the two-minute constraint. Changing it is a decision about what the project is, not a feature — see Changing an invariant.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 3: no server-side database, no accounts, no auth

nodes.label: Invariant 4: everything in the browser has a TTL
nodes.rationale: Drafts and the parsed profile expire after DRAFT_TTL_MS (48h) and are purged on app load, because students use shared computers.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 4: everything in the browser has a ttl

nodes.label: Invariant 5: keys default to sessionStorage
nodes.rationale: localStorage is opt-in behind a 'Remember on this device' toggle with a shared-computer warning, because lab machines are shared.

nodes.label: Invariant 6: no direct DOM manipulation
nodes.rationale: React owns the DOM; mutating it underneath causes bugs that only appear in production builds. Single allowed exception: a detached <a> element for file downloads in drafts/page.tsx.

nodes.label: Invariant 7: prompts must forbid invention
nodes.rationale: Every prompt tells the model not to invent achievements, numbers, companies or skills and to mark gaps as [add number], because students paste the output into real applications.

nodes.label: Invariant 8: no secret in client code or commits
nodes.rationale: Server secrets live in Vercel env vars only and .env* is git-ignored — obvious, but easy to slip.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 8: no secret in client code or commits

nodes.label: Invariant 9: no analytics that capture page content or user input
nodes.rationale: Analytics that record content would contradict the privacy promise documented in docs/PRIVACY.md.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 9: no analytics that capture page content or user input

nodes.label: Invariant 10: don't oversell
nodes.rationale: Copy describes what the app does (polish, draft, check) and never promises replies, interviews or jobs — the app was renamed from 'CareerLift' for exactly this reason.

nodes.label: Invariant 11: never claim something was saved unless storage confirms it
nodes.rationale: A card that read hasKey from the input buffer unmounted the Save button on the first keystroke, so pasting a key looked successful and stored nothing, and every later request failed with a misleading deployment error. Decide UI state from what is stored, never from the value being typed, and surface a failed write instead of swallowing it.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 11: never claim something was saved unless storage confirms it

nodes.label: Invariant 12: anything checkable without a model is checked without one
nodes.rationale: Rule-based results appear instantly, cost nothing, and work before a student has a key; the AI builds on their findings instead of repeating them.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 12: anything checkable without a model is checked without one

nodes.label: Changing an invariant
nodes.rationale: Invariants are hard, not permanent: one may be revisited when the project's goals genuinely change, but that is a deliberate decision made in its own PR, not something a feature quietly assumes. Procedure: say so plainly, amend the table with the new reasoning, and only then build on it; never ship a feature that contradicts a row while the row still stands.

nodes.label: Known candidate: optional accounts with cross-device sync
nodes.rationale: Recorded explicitly so it stops looking like an accident. It would mean accepting server-side storage of student data, real authentication and a host-side cost, moving four things at once: the zero-cost constraint, the two-minute no-account constraint, 'student content stays client-side', and 'no server-side database'. Treat it as a fork in the road, not a backlog item.
nodes.norm_label: known candidate: optional accounts with cross-device sync

nodes.label: Naming rule: refer to a rule by what it says, not only by its number
nodes.rationale: Both the constraint list and the invariant list are numbered, so 'constraint 3' and 'invariant 3' are different rules that read alike — and a number shifts the moment a row is inserted above it.
nodes.norm_label: naming rule: refer to a rule by what it says, not only by its number

nodes.label: The codebase map (graphify-out snapshot)
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ holds graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md and graph.json so a newcomer, human or AI, can see the shape of the project without reading every file. It is a snapshot committed to git, which means it can lie; two honesty rules keep it honest.

nodes.label: Map honesty rule 1: regenerate after a docs change, not alongside one
nodes.rationale: This has already gone wrong once: a graph merged in the same PR as a CLAUDE.md edit was extracted before that edit landed, so the committed map described ten invariants while the file beside it had twelve — and named 'Ten Hard Invariants' as the most connected node in the repo.
nodes.norm_label: map honesty rule 1: regenerate after a docs change, not alongside one

nodes.label: Map honesty rule 2: check one fact before committing it
nodes.rationale: Open GRAPH_REPORT.md, read the top god node, and confirm it matches the code being shipped. A map whose most prominent claim is wrong is worse than no map.
nodes.norm_label: map honesty rule 2: check one fact before committing it

nodes.label: A stale graph is documentation drift, not a build artefact
nodes.rationale: Framing the committed graph as documentation rather than build output makes staleness a review problem rather than something that will fix itself on the next build.
nodes.norm_label: a stale graph is documentation drift, not a build artefact

nodes.label: Pre-merge verification checklist
nodes.rationale: Run before merging any PR including your own, and report results honestly — say a failure rather than merging past it.

nodes.label: Checklist 1: it builds and passes checks
nodes.rationale: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm run build must all pass before merge.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 1: it builds and passes checks

nodes.label: Checklist 2: the invariants still hold
nodes.rationale: For any diff touching src/lib/ai/, src/lib/keys.ts, src/lib/db.ts or the API routes, grep explicitly for apiKey references outside process.env, console.log of request bodies, and dangerouslyAllowBrowser outside providers/.

nodes.label: Checklist 3: no secrets are committed
nodes.rationale: Diff against origin/main and grep for provider key prefixes; the grep must return nothing.

nodes.label: Checklist 4: it works in a browser, not just in CI
nodes.rationale: Every user-visible bug in this repo's history passed tsc, eslint and build: a stuck loading spinner, a mis-parsed PDF section, an error only visible after clicking Generate, a Save button that unmounted as you typed, and an ATS rule that scored a well-written profile at zero. Reading the page's markup is not using it.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 4: it works in a browser, not just in ci

nodes.label: Checklist 4a: check the rendered result, not the edit
nodes.rationale: A find-and-replace that matches nothing reports success and changes nothing; if a change does not appear, suspect a stale build before suspecting the logic.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 4a: check the rendered result, not the edit

nodes.label: Checklist 4b: test on real data, not only on a fixture you wrote
nodes.rationale: The synthetic profile in this repo's history was clean, comma-separated and short; a real LinkedIn export broke the location regex, truncated multi-line headlines, reported 24 roles for six, and used a check-mark glyph as a bullet. Fixtures confirm what you expected; real files find what you did not.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 4b: test on real data, not only on a fixture you wrote

nodes.label: Checklist 5: the no-key path still behaves
nodes.rationale: With no API key saved and no shared key configured, the app must say so up front via SetupBanner rather than failing at the moment of generation.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 5: the no-key path still behaves

nodes.label: Checklist 6: privacy claims still true
nodes.rationale: A change that adds a network call must leave the README privacy table and docs/PRIVACY.md accurate, or update them in the same PR.

nodes.label: Checklist 7: docs updated
nodes.rationale: New feature to the README feature table, new file to the README folder tree, new env var to .env.example and the README deploy table.

nodes.label: Checklist 8: the codebase map is not stale
nodes.rationale: If the PR changed CLAUDE.md, the README or the shape of src/, regenerate graphify-out/ after those edits are final, in a separate commit or PR — extraction reads the files as they were when it started, so a graph built alongside a docs change describes the version before it.
nodes.norm_label: checklist 8: the codebase map is not stale

nodes.label: PR review priority order
nodes.rationale: Be direct about real problems and quiet about style preferences; invariant breaks, leaks and cost regressions outrank everything else. Never merge an unverified PR and never approve because CI is green — CI only checks types, lint and build.

nodes.label: .github/workflows/claude-review.yml (optional automated review)
nodes.rationale: Runs only if an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repository secret exists, so forks are unaffected; it is off by default because it consumes paid API credit from whoever owns the key.

nodes.label: Convention: TypeScript strict, no any
nodes.rationale: No any and no custom types duplicating SDK types.

nodes.label: Convention: Server Components by default
nodes.rationale: Add "use client" only where browser APIs or state are needed.

nodes.label: Convention: browser-only reads happen after hydration
nodes.rationale: Use useIsClient() before reading localStorage/sessionStorage during render, and never call setState synchronously inside useEffect — the lint rule rejects it.
nodes.norm_label: convention: browser-only reads happen after hydration

nodes.label: Convention: provider SDKs are lazy-loaded
nodes.rationale: Lazy loading in client.ts means a Gemini user never downloads the other three provider bundles.

nodes.label: Convention: phones are the default (check at 375px)
nodes.rationale: Most students open this on a phone: navigation must stay reachable, banners small, upload zones must say 'tap' rather than 'drop', and nothing may scroll sideways.
nodes.norm_label: convention: phones are the default (check at 375px)

nodes.label: Convention: model ids go stale
nodes.rationale: config.ts holds a curated list per provider but Settings can fetch the live list with the student's key; when a default stops working, check the provider's docs rather than guessing an id.

nodes.label: Convention: branch and PR for every change
nodes.rationale: main auto-deploys to production, so nothing is committed to main directly.
nodes.norm_label: convention: branch and pr for every change

nodes.label: Convention: never delete a branch without the owner asking
nodes.norm_label: convention: never delete a branch without the owner asking

nodes.norm_label: src/lib/keys.ts (key storage, active provider, device id)

nodes.label: Contributing ground rules
nodes.rationale: A five-point short version of CLAUDE.md, meant to save a contributor a rewrite before they start.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md is the source of truth
nodes.rationale: It lists twelve invariants and the checklist every PR is verified against before merge; reading it takes two minutes and prevents rewrites.
nodes.norm_label: claude.md is the source of truth

nodes.label: Ground rule 1: zero cost stays zero cost
nodes.rationale: Server-side state (databases, auth) is forbidden by invariant 3, not merely discouraged: a feature needing it requires changing that invariant first, in its own PR — see CLAUDE.md, Changing an invariant.
nodes.norm_label: ground rule 1: zero cost stays zero cost

nodes.label: Ground rule 2: privacy is the product
nodes.rationale: Student profiles, resumes, drafts and API keys must never reach the server; BYOK calls go browser to provider, and a change that makes that untrue will not be merged.
nodes.norm_label: ground rule 2: privacy is the product

nodes.label: Ground rule 3: no direct DOM manipulation
nodes.rationale: Drive the UI through React state; the one exception is a detached <a> for downloads.
nodes.norm_label: ground rule 3: no direct dom manipulation

nodes.label: Development setup and pre-PR checks
nodes.rationale: After tsc, lint and build, open the app in a browser and use the thing you changed: CI only checks types, lint and build, and every user-visible bug this project has had passed all three.

nodes.label: Branching (feat/fix/docs, PR against main)
nodes.rationale: main deploys automatically, so it is never committed to directly.

nodes.label: Where things live (task to file map)
nodes.norm_label: where things live (task to file map)

nodes.label: Adding an AI provider
nodes.rationale: Three steps: a providers/<name>.ts exporting StreamFn and ListModelsFn using the vendor SDK with browser access enabled, registration in client.ts loaders and modelListers, and a PROVIDERS entry in config.ts with a curated model list and key URL.

nodes.label: Good first contributions
nodes.rationale: Prompts, ATS rules, trending sources, parser fixes and UI translations are the smallest self-contained changes; ATS rules are pure functions and easy to reason about.

nodes.label: Report security issues via private GitHub advisory
nodes.norm_label: report security issues via private github advisory

nodes.norm_label: you don't need to contribute to use it (mit, fork freely)

nodes.label: ProfilePolish
nodes.author: Kannan
nodes.rationale: A free, private LinkedIn and resume coach for college students: runs in the browser, bring your own free API key, no sign-up, no database, MIT licensed.

nodes.label: Why this exists
nodes.rationale: Most AI LinkedIn tools cost Rs 500-2,000 a month and keep the profile on their servers; students don't need that, so this reads the PDF export LinkedIn already gives you, talks to the provider directly from the browser with the student's own free key, keeps everything local with a 48h auto-clear, and costs the host nothing.

nodes.label: The name is the promise
nodes.rationale: ProfilePolish polishes what the student writes; it does not apply for jobs, contact recruiters, or guarantee interviews, and everything it produces is a draft to read and edit.

nodes.label: Feature: Onboarding (LinkedIn PDF drop or paste)
nodes.norm_label: feature: onboarding (linkedin pdf drop or paste)

nodes.label: Feature: Profile Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Rule-based completeness check first, then the AI review (score, quick wins, headline and About rewrites, bullet rewrites, skills to add); accepts a screenshot for vision models.

nodes.label: Feature: My Drafts (48-hour countdown, Markdown export)
nodes.norm_label: feature: my drafts (48-hour countdown, markdown export)

nodes.label: Feature: Settings (BYOK keys, models, clear all data)
nodes.rationale: Session-only keys by default with an opt-in 'remember on this device', plus one-click 'clear all my data'.
nodes.norm_label: feature: settings (byok keys, models, clear all data)

nodes.label: Getting started (students)
nodes.rationale: On a college lab computer, leave 'Remember my keys' off and click 'Clear all my data' before leaving.

nodes.label: Deploy your own (free)
nodes.rationale: Fork, import into Vercel, optionally add shared-key env vars, deploy. Two small server routes mean it cannot be a purely static site; deleting src/app/api/generate makes a fork BYOK-only.

nodes.label: Shared-key environment variables
nodes.rationale: GEMINI_API_KEY is server-side only and used only for students without their own key; SHARED_DAILY_LIMIT_GLOBAL must stay under the host's Gemini free-tier quota so the deployment never costs money.

nodes.label: Upstash Redis rate limiting (optional)
nodes.rationale: Free Upstash Redis makes the limits reliable across serverless instances; without it, in-memory limits reset whenever Vercel spins up a new instance — fine for a small pilot.

nodes.label: /api/generate shared-key proxy
nodes.rationale: The one server route that touches student prompts: it forwards to Gemini with Cache-Control: no-store and no logging, and applies per-device, IP and global limits.

nodes.label: How it works (browser vs serverless diagram)
nodes.norm_label: how it works (browser vs serverless diagram)

nodes.label: Tech stack (Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, Dexie, pdf.js)
nodes.rationale: Official SDKs for @google/genai, groq-sdk, openai and @anthropic-ai/sdk are each lazy-loaded only when chosen.
nodes.norm_label: tech stack (next.js 16, react 19, tailwind 4, dexie, pdf.js)

nodes.label: Workshop slide deck: From Ghosted to Shortlisted
nodes.rationale: The final slide points students at ProfilePolish so they can do the work straight after the session.

nodes.label: Workshop speaker script
nodes.rationale: The demo that lands best is live: drop a student's own LinkedIn PDF in and read the review aloud — about two minutes, more convincing than any slide.

nodes.label: Fork it and make it your own
nodes.rationale: Built to be forked: rename via APP_NAME/APP_TAGLINE in config.ts, recolour via CSS variables in globals.css, deploy your own instance — no permission needed and nothing has to be contributed back.
nodes.norm_label: fork it and make it your own

nodes.rationale: Most features are one new page plus one new prompt; streaming, copy, save-draft, error handling and BYOK/shared-key routing all come from useGenerate() and OutputPanel, so the AI plumbing is untouched.

nodes.label: README codebase map section
nodes.rationale: Node, edge and community counts are deliberately left at the top of the generated report rather than repeated here, so they cannot drift. Regenerate after a docs edit lands, never in the same pass, or the map describes the version before it.

nodes.label: Privacy model table
nodes.rationale: Direct-from-browser BYOK is chosen because then there is nothing on the server that can leak; the only secret the server holds is the host's own shared key. The one identifier sent to the server is an anonymous device id header used to rate-limit the shared key fairly.

nodes.label: BYOK: bring your own free key, called direct from the browser
nodes.norm_label: byok: bring your own free key, called direct from the browser

nodes.label: Model defaults per provider
nodes.rationale: Model ids change every few months, so the 'Load models from ...' button pulls the live list with the student's key and the dropdown never goes stale.

nodes.label: Limitation: no LinkedIn API, heuristic PDF parsing
nodes.rationale: LinkedIn does not let apps read profiles, so the PDF export is the supported path; the parser is heuristic, but the AI always reads the full extracted text so a mis-detected name does not hurt the suggestions.
nodes.norm_label: limitation: no linkedin api, heuristic pdf parsing

nodes.label: Roadmap: cross-device sync
nodes.rationale: Genuinely useful but explicitly not a drop-in feature: it needs accounts and server-side storage, which CLAUDE.md's invariant 3 forbids today. Doing it means deliberately changing that invariant first and accepting that student data would leave the browser — only worth it if students actually ask.

nodes.label: Roadmap: cover-letter generator
nodes.rationale: Would reuse the existing resume plus job-description pipeline.

nodes.rationale: Contact info, standard headings, length, action verbs, metrics, cliches, table/column artefacts and keyword match against a pasted job description — all before any AI call.
